name: Basalt Echo

detectability.signature: Repeating tachyon burst pattern with a fixed 47-minute period, accompanied by faint chronometric distortion field

proximity: Chronometers drift by 0.3 seconds per hour, always gaining
Crew report brief moments of déjà vu that intensify near the boundary
Communication signals experience minor temporal echoes, arriving twice with a 47-minute delay
contact: All timepieces synchronize to the anomaly's 47-minute cycle regardless of their mechanism
Crew experience vivid flashes of events that will occur within the next loop iteration
Ship logs begin recording entries with timestamps from previous cycles
prolonged_exposure: Personnel lose the ability to distinguish current experiences from temporal echoes
Ship systems begin executing command sequences from previous loop iterations
Biological processes slow as local time dilates, aging approximately one hour for every three elapsed

behavior.cycle: Complete temporal reset every 47 minutes, 12 seconds

phenomena: Ghost images of objects from previous loop iterations are faintly visible, layered like geological strata
Sound transmitted through the boundary arrives as a deep, resonant hum reminiscent of stone vibrating
Small objects released into the anomaly reappear at their entry point exactly 47 minutes later
The boundary shimmers with a dark, vitreous sheen that observers consistently describe as looking like polished basalt
hazards: Prolonged exposure causes temporal disassociation, making it impossible to determine which iteration of events is current
Ship navigation computers cannot reconcile loop-reset positional data, leading to cascading errors
opportunities: The predictable loop allows controlled study of temporal mechanics with minimal risk at the boundary
Objects preserved within the loop remain in stasis between resets, offering perfect preservation
The time dilation effect at the boundary could be leveraged for accelerated external observation
known_incidents: Research station Epoch-7 operated at the boundary for fourteen months, producing groundbreaking papers on chronometric theory before the crew requested reassignment due to persistent temporal disassociation symptoms.
A courier drone entered the anomaly in 2507 and continues to emerge every 47 minutes carrying the same message, now considered the longest-running unintentional temporal experiment on record.
description: Basalt Echo manifests as a dark, perfectly spherical region of space with a surface that gleams like polished volcanic glass. Its boundary is sharp and well-defined, a black mirror reflecting starlight with a faint temporal shimmer that makes the reflections arrive moments before the light itself. At 780 kilometers in radius, it is small enough to circumnavigate in hours but dense enough in temporal distortion to swallow days from the unwary.

Every 47 minutes and 12 seconds, the anomaly pulses, and everything within its boundary resets to its state at the beginning of the cycle. Objects, energy patterns, and even photons snap back to their prior positions like a geological stratum being re-deposited. The effect is perfectly predictable, making Basalt Echo one of the most studied temporal anomalies in known space. At the boundary, time flows unevenly, and crew members report hearing a deep harmonic vibration they describe as the sound of the universe remembering itself.

Analysis of the anomaly's tachyon signature suggests it formed approximately 890 million years ago, likely the result of a rare stellar collapse that created a self-sustaining temporal eddy in local spacetime. The name derives from early survey reports that described the anomaly's visual appearance and cyclical nature as resembling layers of cooled volcanic rock, each cycle a new stratum laid atop the last. The comparison proved more apt than intended when researchers discovered that faint ghost-images from previous cycles accumulate visually, like translucent geological layers.

Basalt Echo remains a moderate navigational hazard, primarily to small craft that might blunder into its boundary without adequate chronometric sensors. The scientific community maintains a rotating observation post at a safe distance, and the anomaly features in the curriculum of every major temporal physics program. The courier drone that entered in 2507 has become something of a local landmark, its punctual 47-minute appearances a reliable feature of the region that passing ships sometimes stop to witness.
